title: Served HTTP submits are in-memory only — the durable ledgers fsync persistence is inert on the served surface
repro: serve-studio → 9 HTTP submits → /health trials:10 but data/studio/live-ledger.jsonl stays 1 line; a restart loses all served submits. serve-studio mounts routes with durable.store (inner in-memory Store), so submit_spec calls store.register (RAM) not durable.register (fsync).
evidence: wc -l live-ledger.jsonl = 1 after 10 in-memory trials; serve-studio.ts:85 mountable(durable.store,...); durable.register (fsync) never on the route path

title: Served HTTP submits are in-memory only — the durable ledgers fsync persistence is inert on the served surface
repro: serve-studio → 9 HTTP submits → /health trials:10 but data/studio/live-ledger.jsonl stays 1 line; a restart loses all served submits. serve-studio mounts routes with durable.store (inner in-memory Store), so submit_spec calls store.register (RAM) not durable.register (fsync).
evidence: wc -l live-ledger.jsonl = 1 after 10 in-memory trials; serve-studio.ts:85 mountable(durable.store,...); durable.register (fsync) never on the route path
resolution: architectural + needs a product decision — parked, not fixed speculatively

park.rationale: Whether anonymous served submits SHOULD durably persist is a genuine product/security decision, not a mechanical fix. Persisting every anonymous submit to the committed record is an abuse/pollution vector; keeping them ephemeral is a defensible demo-safety choice. The right fix (persist to an ISOLATED, authn-gated durable file, separate from the authored live-ledger) needs design, not a one-line wiring swap.
park.impact: Affects only the SERVED demo surface. The AUTHORED pipeline (live-run, capture, enrollment) already uses durable.register (fsync) and is unaffected — L-PERSIST holds where it is load-bearing. A demo visitor who submits and restarts the server loses their in-memory trial; no verdict is wrong, nothing is laundered (the deflation still counts the in-memory family within the session).
park.nextSteps: Decide the persistence policy: (a) ephemeral-by-design (document it on the dashboard/SKILL.md), or (b) persist served submits to data/studio/served-submissions.jsonl via a durable-wrapping store, gated behind the Bearer credential + rate limits, isolated from the authored live-ledger. Add a wall proving served submits survive a restart under option (b).
park.targetSprint: the next STUDIO sprint (served-persistence policy), alongside sybil-economics (both are served-surface abuse/policy questions)
